page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0, placing it in the top tier of tested servers. Single-threaded operations perform exceptionally well, with gzip compression reaching 34.85 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 15.13 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. Stress-ng multi-core performance and uncached memory read/write bandwidth fall into the lower percentiles, reflecting a bottleneck when workloads scale across all threads or demand high memory throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a specialized compute-to-memory ratio designed for workloads that prioritize raw single-threaded CPU speed over massive memory footprints. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets, such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, enhances its utility for lightweight vector calculations and small-scale machine learning inference. This server is recommended for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, Redis key-value operations, and basic text processing workloads that do not require extensive memory capacity or local storage.
